jobs.title: spec.py: schema, defaults, validate
jobs.task:
Goal
talk_to_cad/spec.py passes tests/test_spec.py: FAMILIES, DEFAULTS, SpecError(.missing), validate(spec) -> new normalized dict.

Facts (already verified)
The schema, required dims, defaults and rejection rules are in PLAN.md 'Spec schema v1' and 'Coordinate conventions'.
tests/test_spec.py is the exact contract; read it first. checks/golden.json has 8 specs that must validate unchanged.

Do
1. Read tests/test_spec.py and PLAN.md spec section.
2. Write talk_to_cad/spec.py:
   FAMILIES = ("plate","cylinder","washer","box","bracket")
   DEFAULTS = {"plate": {"corner_radius": 0}, "cylinder": {"inner_d": 0}, "washer": {}, "box": {"wall": 2.4}, "bracket": {}}
   class SpecError(ValueError) with attribute .missing (list of missing required dim names, [] otherwise).
   validate(spec): deep-copy input; check family; require a non-empty string name and normalise it to snake_case
   (lowercase, runs of non [a-z0-9] -> '_', strip '_'); require all required dims (raise SpecError with .missing listing
   ALL missing names); coerce dims to float, reject bool/str; fill defaults; box.floor defaults to wall; reject
   non-positive dims (corner_radius and cylinder.inner_d may be 0); apply every rejection rule in PLAN.md; normalise hole
   lists (plate: holes; bracket: holes_a, holes_b; always present as lists, each entry {d, x, y} floats, d > 0, fully on
   its face, bracket holes clear of the corner: x - d/2 >= thickness). Return {"spec_version": 1, "family", "name", "dims", holes...}.
3. Run python -m pytest tests/test_spec.py -q until green.

jobs.title: build.py + plate family + STL/3MF export

Goal

checks/check_mesh.py is what the test runs on the output: bbox within 0.05 mm, part centred in XY sitting on Z=0,

CadQuery: Workplane("XY").box(L, W, T, centered=(True, True, False)) gives a centred box on Z=0.

wp = wp.faces(">Z").workplane(centerOption="ProjectedOrigin").pushPoints([(x, y)]).hole(d)  (hole() cuts through everything).
Export: from cadquery import exporters; exporters.export(wp, stl_path, exportType="STL", tolerance=0.01, angularTolerance=0.1)
then trimesh.load(stl_path, force="mesh").export(mf_path)  writes the 3MF from the same tessellation.

jobs.title: bracket family (L-bracket)
jobs.task:
Goal
bracket passes its geometry tests, then the whole family suite is green.

Facts (already verified)
Coordinates in PLAN.md: outer corner at the ORIGIN (not centred). Leg A: Workplane("XY").box(leg_a, width, t, centered=False)
(x 0..leg_a, y 0..width, z 0..t). Leg B: Workplane("XY").box(t, width, leg_b, centered=False). wp = legA.union(legB).
Holes by explicit cutters, not face selection:
  leg A hole {d,x,y}: cutter = Workplane("XY").center(x, y).circle(d/2).extrude(t);  wp = wp.cut(cutter)
  leg B hole {d,x,y}: cutter = Workplane("YZ").center(y, x).circle(d/2).extrude(t);  wp = wp.cut(cutter)
  (Workplane("YZ") normal is +X, local coordinates are (y, z); extrude(t) runs from x=0 to x=t.)
check_mesh sections at z=t/2 (plane x,y: leg A holes) and x=t/2 (plane y,z: leg B holes). Analytic volume = legA + legB - t*t*width - holes.

jobs.title: Preview renderer (PIL + numpy painter's algorithm)
jobs.task:
Goal
talk_to_cad/preview.py renders a readable isometric PNG with the dimensions on it, and the whole golden set passes checks/run_golden.py (spec mode).

Facts (already verified)
No OpenGL, pyrender, matplotlib or Blender: PIL + numpy + trimesh only. checks/check_preview.py requires >= 800x600,
non-blank, object covering 2-90% of the frame. Target 1200x900, white background.
Isometric orthographic view: rotate the mesh so the view direction is (1, 1, 1) -> e.g. rotate about Z by -45 deg then about X by
-35.264 deg, then drop the depth axis. Painter's algorithm: sort triangles by mean depth, draw far to near with ImageDraw.polygon.
Lambert shading: shade = 0.35 + 0.65 * max(0, dot(normal, light)) with light = normalised (0.3, 0.4, 0.85) in view space;
base colour (120, 160, 220); outline each triangle in the same fill colour so edges don't show. Fit the part with a 10% margin.

   'L x W x H mm' from the spec dims (plate: length x width x thickness; cylinder/washer: outer_d x outer_d x height/thickness;
   box: length x width x height; bracket: leg_a x width x leg_b) and one line per hole ('hole d=5 at (-20, 0)').

jobs.title: LLM: description -> spec (prompt, parser, CLI description mode)
jobs.task:
Goal
talk_to_cad/llm.py passes tests/test_llm_parse.py and python -m talk_to_cad "<description>" works against the local Ollama model.

Facts (already verified)
Endpoint: OpenAI-compatible POST to env TALK_TO_CAD_LLM_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions) with
{"model": env TALK_TO_CAD_LLM_MODEL, "messages": [...], "temperature": 0, "stream": false}; use urllib.request, 120 s timeout.
Qwen may wrap JSON in ``` fences and emit <think>...</think>; strip both. The model must NEVER invent a number: if a required dim
is missing it must answer {"missing": ["question", ...]}. tests/test_llm_parse.py and tests/fixtures/llm_outputs/ are the exact
contract for build_messages and parse_model_output; checks/golden.json gives 8 description->spec pairs to use as few-shot examples
(use 4 of them as examples; the live check later uses all 8, so the prompt must generalise, not memorise).
The CLI flow: describe_to_spec(description, ask) -> spec; ask=None (or --no-ask) means a {"missing"} answer is an error (exit 3)
instead of a prompt. Default ask = input() once per question, then re-call the model with followups appended.

Do
1. Write talk_to_cad/llm.py:
   SYSTEM prompt (one string): the five families with their required dims and defaults, the coordinate conventions, the
   literal words 'never invent' a number, 'mm', the key names corner_radius, inner_d, holes, holes_a, holes_b, wall, floor,
   the {"missing": [...]} rule, 'JSON only', plus 4 few-shot example pairs from checks/golden.json.
   build_messages(description, followups=None) -> [system, user, (assistant missing-json, user answer)*]; last message is the user.
   parse_model_output(text): strip <think> blocks and fences, find the first balanced {...} that json.loads, return
   {"missing": [...]} as-is or spec.validate(obj); raise LLMParseError on no JSON or on SpecError.
   describe_to_spec(description, ask=input, max_rounds=3).
